interface.title: Nanoindentation explorer (nanoDMA depth-profile explorer)
interface.field: Materials science / nanomechanics (nanoindentation of irradiated and unirradiated material)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory analysis and quality control of raw instrument exports, then export for downstream statistics and figures
interface.what_it_is_for: Load many Hysitron/Bruker nanoDMA *_DYN.txt depth-profile exports, read sample/fluence/grain/measurement from their file names, plot storage modulus, hardness or contact depth against depth as single indents or as group mean/median ± std/SEM, and export the plotted curves and summary tables.

data.note: All 8 test files were uploaded together through the sidebar uploader. The six s##_f##_g##_###_DYN.txt files were decoded correctly. control_sample_A.txt shows '?' metadata and a bare-name label. unreadable_DYN.txt was counted in 'Loaded 8 file(s)' with 4 points and all-'?' metadata, and when ticked it crashed the plot with a KeyError traceback (screens/004.webp, screens/005.webp). The reviewer traced this to the parser: the file's line 'Test type: Basic hardness, modulus' passes the loose header check (app.py:104), so the file is accepted as valid but has no usable columns. This is a synthetic file meeting a lenient parser, not missing error reporting. Unticking its Show box cleared the error (screens/007.webp). Changing a filter re-ticked it (screens/021.webp), so I removed it from the uploader (screens/022.webp) and worked with the other 7 files from then on.

features.name: Filename-convention metadata decoder with selection table
features.general: Turn a batch of uploaded measurement files into a table whose descriptive fields (specimen, treatment level, subregion, replicate number) are parsed from a naming pattern. Names that do not match fall back to an unknown label. Each row has a checkbox that includes or excludes that file from analysis.
features.specific: Upload *_DYN.txt files. Names like s40_f46_g15_000 fill the Sample/Fluence/Grain/Meas. columns, with Points counts; non-matching files show '?'. Tick Show to put a curve in the plot. A file that passes the loose header check but has no usable columns still loads (4 points, all '?') and raises a KeyError when shown. Show ticks reset to ticked when a filter changes.
steps: Upload many files at once in the sidebar
Read the decoded Sample/Fluence/Grain/Meas./Points columns
Untick Show on a row to drop that file from the plot
Re-tick to restore it
serves_tasks: Load many instrument export files at once
Check that metadata parsed from file names is correct
Exclude an anomalous measurement
Deal with a file that cannot be parsed

features.name: Faceted multiselect filters
features.general: Narrow a dataset with one multi-choice filter per descriptive field. Each filter lists every value found and can be widened back to all values in one step. The plot, table and exports follow the filtered subset.
features.specific: Filter samples / Filter fluences / Filter grains, plus Filter groups once custom groups exist. Chips are removed with x and restored from the dropdown or with 'Select all' (offered only when more than one value is missing). The plot title count and the ZIP button count update.
steps: Remove value chips to narrow a field
Watch the selection table and plot title count update
Open the dropdown and pick values or Select all to widen again
Combine filters across fields
serves_tasks: Narrow to a subset of specimens by any recorded field, then widen again

features.name: Custom group builder with per-group tabs
features.general: Make named groups from whatever measurements are currently shown. Each group gets its own tab listing its members, which can be ticked on or off individually or disbanded; one button clears all groups. The groups then become a grouping key for aggregation.
features.specific: Type a Group name, press '➕ Add shown to group'. Tabs 'Ungrouped (n)', 'control (3)', 'irradiated (3)' appear, a Filter groups multiselect appears, and Group by switches to 'Custom group'. Each tab has '🗑️ Disband “name”'; the Ungrouped tab has '🗑️ Clear all groups'. A group created after the first is not added to Filter groups automatically.
steps: Filter the table to the files wanted
Type a group name and press ➕ Add shown to group
Repeat for a second group and add it to Filter groups
Open a group tab to tick or untick members
Disband one group or Clear all groups
serves_tasks: Build custom groups that cut across predefined subgroups
Compare the averaged curves of two custom groups
See how robust a group average is to an outlier

features.name: Binned depth-profile aggregation (mean/median ± std/SEM bands)
features.general: Plot many replicate curves either individually or as one central curve per group with a shaded spread band. The user picks the measured property, the statistic (mean or median), the spread (std or SEM), the grouping key and how many bins the depth axis is resampled into. The legend shows n per group.
features.specific: Plot mode radio: Per measurement / Mean ± std / Median ± std / Mean ± SEM / Median ± SEM per group. 'Group by' chooses Grain or Custom group, the 'Depth bins' slider runs from 20 to 400, and Quantity (Y) is Storage modulus, Hardness or Contact depth. Per-group modes always use contact depth as the X axis. Hover shows the value and std.

screens_never_reached: A sidebar list of files that failed to parse. It never showed unreadable_DYN.txt, because that file's line 'Test type: Basic hardness, modulus' passes the loose header check (app.py:104, per the reviewer). So it loaded as valid (4 points, '?' metadata) with no usable columns, and plotting it raised an uncaught KeyError traceback in the main panel (screens/005.webp). This comes from the synthetic file meeting a lenient parser; whether the error list works for a file that fails the header check was not tested.
A per-custom-group summary table: the Summary statistics section only offers per-measurement rows and 'Averages per grain', with no group column (screens/046.webp)
not_done: I could not read either downloaded ZIP of plotted curves (0296e64a…zip, e01343b9…zip). The download reader answered 'no download' for these names, so I did not check the per-curve CSV contents or the binning against the plot.
The selection table's built-in 'Download as CSV' icon produced no download that I could see (screens/059.webp), so exporting the decoded metadata table is unverified.

I only tried X axis 'Measurement point #' while Plot mode was Median ± SEM per group, where the ticks stayed at contact depths ≈120–200 (screens/019.webp). This is intended: per-group modes always use contact depth (app.py:632-633; the page says 'Group aggregation always uses contact depth as the X axis', check/screens/040.webp). The point-index axis (0–11) in Per measurement mode is shown only by the replay (check/screens/041.webp).

unreadable_DYN.txt was accepted by the loose header check, crashed the plot when shown, and was re-ticked whenever a filter changed (screens/021.webp), so I removed it from the uploader for the rest of the run.

A newly created second custom group ('control') was not added to Filter groups automatically. It was hidden from the plot until I added it by hand (screens/041.webp, screens/042.webp). After 'control' was disbanded, its chip stayed in Filter groups (screens/056.webp).

Median versus mean robustness for the control group could not be shown cleanly at the outlier depth. The median there equals the mean of only 2 indents (4.385 GPa), which suggests g21's blank rows fall in that bin. I did not confirm this from the exported data, because I could not read the ZIP.
I compared irradiated and control groups only for hardness; no storage-modulus comparison between them was made, although the goal names it.
I did not clear a filter completely, so the 'No measurements selected' warning was never seen.

I clicked the '(ungrouped) control_sample_A' legend entry, box-zoomed and double-clicked to reset (screens/049.webp, screens/050.webp); the legend toggle did not seem to restore the hidden trace after the reset. These are the chart library's built-in controls, not a step of this tool's work, and I did not look into it further.
